value.rationale: For CTMC transition integrators, entrywise nonnegativity is required to preserve probabilistic meaning and is not implied by stable eigenvalues. The complete exact rate-dependent positivity horizon for an infinite family of reversible but nonuniform stars, together with a minimal stable/nonpositive witness, provides a natural reusable numerical-analysis boundary. Its univariate cubic certificates are not merely a textbook scalar stability computation.
residual_risks: Independent finite computations are checks only; global cutoff follows monotonicity and spectral reasoning.

final_claim: For every bidirected-star CTMC row generator Q with m>=1 and arbitrary a_j,b_j>0, completed classical RK4 P(h)=sum_{k=0}^4 h^k Q^k/k! is entrywise nonnegative exactly for 0<=h<=min_j h_j, where each h_j is the unique positive root of the explicit strictly decreasing cubic g_j(h). The only possible sign loss is hub–leaf; all leaf–leaf off-diagonal and all diagonal entries stay positive for all h>0. A 3-state reversible nonuniform chain has RK4 spectral stability despite negative transitions and is minimal in state count.
limitations: All edge rates strictly positive; the result is not claimed for general trees, nonlinear SSP, or intermediate stages.
